title: Missing X-Frame-Options Header
evidence: The 'X-Frame-Options' header was missing from the HTTP response headers.
technical_explanation: Without X-Frame-Options, the application can be framed by malicious sites, exposing it to clickjacking.
plain_explanation: Your website can be invisibly loaded inside another malicious website, tricking users into clicking unintended buttons.
remediation: Configure your web server to return the 'X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN' header.

title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) Header
evidence: The 'Strict-Transport-Security' header was missing from the HTTP response headers.
technical_explanation: HSTS enforces secure HTTPS connections, preventing protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.
plain_explanation: Users could initially connect over an unencrypted connection, making their data vulnerable to interception.
remediation: Configure your web server to include 'Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains'.

title: HTTP Not Redirecting to HTTPS
evidence: Accessing 'http://example.com' did not enforce a redirect to HTTPS (final destination: http://example.com/).
technical_explanation: The web server permits cleartext HTTP communication without enforcing a secure HTTPS redirect.
plain_explanation: Users who type your web address without 'https://' can be vulnerable to interception or traffic modification.
remediation: Configure your web server to permanently redirect all incoming HTTP traffic to HTTPS (using a 301 redirect).
